about_page_description: Game audio designer. Piano kid turned physics nerd turned C++ programmer. Now building spatial audio for VR/AR training sims.
hook: Classical piano, then maths and physics, now C++ and Wwise. I build game audio from both sides: the sound and the code.
intro_sub: Belgium · DAE Howest · Technical sound design · XR Labs
background_1: Hi, I'm Igor. I started with classical piano, moved to maths and physics, and ended up in game development. Along the way I figured out that making audio for games is where all three connect.
background_2: Music trained my ears. Maths taught me to think in systems. Put those together and you get someone who records foley in the morning and debugs C++ in the afternoon.
background_3: Three years at DAE in Kortrijk. C++, C#, Unity, Unreal, Wwise. But the shipped projects taught me more than the lectures. At some point you stop wanting to study games and start wanting to ship them.
approach_1: At XR Labs I lead technical sound design for VR/AR training sims. Police, military, customs. People who need the audio to feel real, because they're training for situations that are.
approach_2: The best part is watching someone put on a headset and react to something I made. If the gunshot echo doesn't match the room, they'll tell you. Real users don't care about your reverb settings. They care if it sounds right.
approach_3: That's why I put so much time into Steam Audio: reflections, transmission, material absorption. In VR, if the acoustics are off, people know in seconds.
cta_text: Working on a game or VR/AR project and need audio? Let's talk.
